newsitem.title: JAPAN: ZELENSKAYA WINS SECOND HAKUBA DOWNHILL.
newsitem.headline: ZELENSKAYA WINS SECOND HAKUBA DOWNHILL.

text.p: Russia's Varvara Zelenskaya won the second women's alpine skiing world cup downhill on Sunday in a time of 1 minute 35.64 seconds according to unofficial results.
Prenilla Wiberg of Sweden was second at 1:36.09 and Renate Goetschl of Austria was third at 1:36.11.

Varvara Zelenskaya took the lead in the world cup downhill rankings on a bright, sunny Sunday morning on Hakuba's 2657 metre-long, 781 metre vertical drop downhill course which will be used for the 1998 Nagano Winter Olympics.
Sunday's win is the Russian skiier's third consecutive world cup downhill victory following wins at Laax in Switzerland earlier this month and on Friday on the same Hakuba course.
Sunday's victory was the fourth win of Zelenskaya's career but she said she was not confident of success before the start.
"I was really nervous today but I tried not to think about the skiing I could show," she said.

World cup overall leader, Prenilla Wiberg of Sweden, who finished 0.45 seconds slower than Zelenskaya's one minute 35.64 seconds, said she was determined to take a downhill title because it was the only discipline she had yet to win.
